Answer: A
Reason: The combination of spontaneous chest pain, neck swelling (subcutaneous emphysema), and pneumomediastinum immediately following an alcoholic binge (suggesting vomiting/retching) is the classic presentation of Boerhaave syndrome, or esophageal perforation. While alveolar rupture can cause pneumomediastinum, the specific history of forceful emesis makes esophageal rupture the most likely and critical diagnosis to identify.
